extracted.intended_audience: USPTO examiners, patent applicants, practitioners, and stakeholders interested in AI-assisted inventions
extracted.subtask_description: USPTO guidance for determining inventorship and patentability when inventions are created by humans with assistance from AI systems, including examples and instructions for examiners and applicants on assessing the sufficiency of human contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: AI-assisted inventions are not categorically unpatentable
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidance makes clear that AI-assisted inventions are not categorically unpatentable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO states: 'AI-assisted inventions are not categorically unpatentable.' The guidance embraces the use of AI in innovation and signals that use of AI alone does not preclude patent protection; patentability is assessed under existing legal standards focusing on human contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significant human contribution required for patentability/inventorship
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the human contribution to an innovation is significant enough to qualify for a patent when AI also contributed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance instructs examiners and applicants to assess 'whether the human contribution to an innovation is significant enough to qualify for a patent when AI also contributed.' It explicitly states: 'patent protection may be sought for inventions in which a human provided a significant contribution to the invention.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply existing inventorship framework to AI-assisted cases
rubrics_metrics.description: Build on the existing inventorship framework when deciding inventorship for inventions created by humans with assistance from AI systems.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The guidance 'builds on the existing inventorship framework by providing instructions to examiners and applicants on determining the correct inventor(s) to be named in a patent or patent application for inventions created by humans with the assistance of one or more AI systems.' Practically, examiners should use established inventorship principles while accounting for the role and extent of human contribution in AI-assisted developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Determination of correct inventor(s) when AI assisted
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide instructions to determine the correct inventor(s) to be named in a patent or patent application for inventions created by humans with assistance from AI.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO guidance supplies instructions to examiners and applicants on how to 'determin[e] the correct inventor(s) to be named' in cases where AI systems contributed. This implies evaluating who contributed the inventive conception (human actors) versus contributions attributable to AI tools, using the guidance's tests and examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance awarding protection with not locking up future innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Strike a balance between awarding patent protection to promote human ingenuity and investment while not unnecessarily locking up innovation for future developments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As stated by the USPTO Director: the guidance 'strikes a balance between awarding patent protection to promote human ingenuity and investment for AI-assisted inventions while not unnecessarily locking up innovation for future developments.' Examiners and policymakers should weigh incentives for disclosure and investment against overbroad protection that could impede subsequent innovation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of examples and supplemental resources to apply guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult USPTO-provided hypothetical examples and AI-related resources to understand and apply the inventorship guidance in concrete situations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement notes that 'examples of hypothetical situations of how the guidance would apply are available on our AI-related resources webpage.' Applicants and examiners are encouraged to review those examples to clarify how the guidance should be applied to specific fact patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity for public comment and stakeholder engagement
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO will accept public comments on the inventorship guidance and examples until May 13, 2024; stakeholders can attend a public webinar and read supporting materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO invites stakeholders to 'learn more... and provide feedback' via a public webinar and to submit comments as instructed in the Federal Register Notice. This procedural window is part of the rollout and may influence final practices or clarifications.
